root_cause: Keyboard navigation in Pikaday adjusts the date by a fixed increment without skipping disabled days (e.g., weekends) defined by disableDayFn, causing ArrowRight to land on a disabled date.
repair_strategy: Modify the adjustDate method to step day-by-day in the requested direction, checking min/max dates, disableWeekends, and disableDayFn, and stop on the first enabled date before calling setDate.
expected_accessibility_effect: Arrow right/left navigation will now skip weekends, allowing keyboard users to move only between selectable weekdays while preserving the other date, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 keyboard accessibility.
functional_risks: If all dates within the range are disabled, the loop will terminate after maxIter iterations and set the date to the boundary value, which may still be disabled.
Performance impact is negligible for typical use; worst-case iteration is limited to a year's worth of days.
Relies on correct configuration of disableWeekends and disableDayFn; if those are misconfigured, skipping behavior may be unexpected.
verification_requirements: Press ArrowRight from a Friday (e.g., 2026-10-23) and verify the date advances to the following Monday (2026-10-26).
Press ArrowLeft from a Tuesday (e.g., 2026-10-27) and verify the date moves to the previous Friday (2026-10-23).
Confirm that clicking a weekday with the pointer still selects it correctly.
Ensure that minDate and maxDate constraints are still respected when navigating with arrow keys.
When disableDayFn is not set, verify that arrow navigation behaves as originally (day increments).
